E.name: Execute-first
E.text:
The reply length has been changed from brief to detailed for this session.

That means answers will now include the key point, the supporting explanation, and a relevant example or steps, rather than the key point alone.

You can continue with your active recall question, and the next answer will follow the detailed structure.

A.name: Always-ask
A.text:
Next time, practise active recall in smaller steps: retrieve one short piece of information at a time, then check the source and correct the gap before moving on.

Forgetting most of a large answer is normal when the prompt is too broad; it overloads working memory and gives you little to correct. Narrowing the target makes each retrieval attempt succeed or fail clearly, so the feedback step actually strengthens the memory. Checking immediately after retrieval also prevents repeated errors from becoming entrenched.

Example: instead of trying to recall an entire topic, write one question such as 'What are the three stages of this process?' Answer from memory, then open your notes and compare. Note the missing stage, close the notes, and try the same question again a few minutes later. Repeat with a new question once the first is solid.
